name: Slack
label: works in your workspace, ships to theirs
summary: Building is quick and distribution is a toggle. The unknown is the Marketplace review, which Slack publishes no timeline for.
verdict: An afternoon to build, then a toggle to ship. What you can't plan around is Slack's Marketplace review, which has no published timeline.
blocker: Some customer workspaces only allow admin-approved or Marketplace-listed apps, and Slack gives no review timeline.

steps.title: Create the app in the Slack app dashboard
steps.detail: Start from scratch and attach it to a development workspace. The creation click-path wasn't in the pages we read; this step is from how the dashboard works in practice.

steps.title: Add HTTPS redirect URLs
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions. Slack requires SSL for redirect URLs. You can also pass redirect_uri in the authorize request.

fields.label: Match rule
fields.value: https, equal to or under a configured URL, no #

steps.title: Choose bot scopes and user scopes separately
steps.detail: Bot scopes go in scope, user scopes in user_scope. Ask for the minimum, because workspace admins weigh the list when approving.

steps.title: Implement the install flow
steps.detail: Redirect to authorize, check state on return, then exchange the code through oauth.v2.access. The code expires after ten minutes.

steps.title: Activate public distribution
steps.detail: Manage Distribution, Share Your App with Other Workspaces, finish the checklist, Activate Public Distribution. You get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL.

steps.title: Customer admins may have to approve the install
steps.detail: Some workspaces limit installs to admins or to Marketplace-listed apps. The wait is theirs, and nobody has published a number.

steps.title: Optional: submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Reviewed against Slack's requirements and guidelines. Recommended for commercial distribution. The distribution page states no review timeline.

nuances.text: Scopes are additive. Re-authorizing adds them, and removing one means revoking the token.
The team parameter is a hint Slack may drop. Read team.id and is_enterprise_install from the oauth.v2.access response.
Tokens don't expire unless you enable rotation, which is available to apps with granular permissions.
With several redirect URLs configured, send the same redirect_uri on authorize and on the token call, or you get bad_redirect_uri.
Apps with scopes beyond bot, incoming-webhook, commands and identify are uninstalled if the installing user leaves or becomes a guest.
Once published to the Marketplace you can't switch public distribution off. You discontinue the listing instead.

nuances.note: Looked on the distribution page. Review guidelines are linked there but weren't summarized.

blockers.cause: Several redirect URLs are configured and the authorize and token calls sent different ones, or none.
blockers.fix: Send the identical redirect_uri in both calls.

blockers.cause: Someone outside the development workspace tried to install an app that isn't distributed yet.
blockers.fix: Finish the distribution checklist and activate public distribution.

blockers.cause: Optional scopes can be declined during install.
blockers.fix: Check the granted scopes before you show a feature.

blockers.symptom: Admin says they can't install it
blockers.cause: Their workspace restricts installs to approved or listed apps.
blockers.fix: Send the admin your exact scope list and why each is needed.

you: Create the app and the development workspace
Decide whether the Marketplace is worth a review you can't time

redirect.rule: HTTPS only. redirect_uri must equal or sit under a configured URL, with no # fragment.

submission: Request only the scopes you need
SSL on redirect, event, interactivity and slash command URLs
An onboarding flow, since you can't hand-hold every workspace
Marketplace listing is optional but recommended for commercial apps
